name: Voyager — Search p95 under 800 ms
description:
The proportion of time over a 7-day rolling window during which the search p95 latency monitor was not alerting, against a 99.0% objective (01-PRD.md § 6.2).

A monitor-based SLO measures time, not requests. Every minute [Voyager] voyager-search p95 latency above 800 ms spends in the alert state is a minute of budget spent, regardless of how many searches happened in it. That makes the 800 ms threshold on that monitor part of this SLO's definition: widening it to stop the alerting would silently move the objective, which is the main way a monitor-based SLO gets quietly falsified.

A single monitor is used rather than several because Datadog treats a multi-monitor SLO as breached whenever any of them alerts, and mixing latency with error-rate monitors would produce a number that means neither one thing nor the other.

Burn-rate alerts are not attached here. Datadog does not offer them on monitor-based SLOs; the error-budget alerts live on Voyager — Booking success rate instead.
